title: Difficulties in tracking employment outcomes,skill gaps, and the impact of skilling initiatives
department: Maharashtra State Innovation Society, Department of Skills, Employment, Entrepreneurship and Innovation
description:
• Problem Description Training systems frequently capture enrolment, attendance, assessment and certification, but reliable information on employment, self-employment, job retention, wage progression, relevance of training and longer-term livelihood outcomes may remain incomplete.Trainees may change phone numbers or locations, employers may not report consistently, and multiple programmes may use different identifiers and definitions. Without longitudinal outcomes, it is difficult to compare providers, improve courses, target future investments or demonstrate public value. The challenge is to establish credible, low-burden and privacy conscious outcome tracking.
• Expected Solution / Outcome A longitudinal skilling-outcomes and impact-measurement system that creates consent-based trainee records,links training with placement and employment signals, conducts automated and assisted follow-ups,captures self-employment and apprenticeship outcomes, validates employer information, measures wage and retention progression, and provides cohort, course, provider, district and demographic analytics. It should identify skill gaps and reasons for non-placement or attrition. Expected outcomes include higher-quality outcome data, better programme and provider accountability,targeted remedial actions, improved resource allocation and evidence-based policy design.
summary: Innovation (2/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a smart education problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (4/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a working prototype is realistic in a 36-hour window. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Education. Tech Depth (1/5): centers on moderate engineering scope. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 16/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Tracking Employment Outcomes, Skill Gaps, and Impact of Skilling Initiatives

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a consent-based system that follows trainees after they finish a skilling programme, tracking whether they actually got jobs, how their wages progressed, and how long they stayed employed, so training providers and policymakers get real evidence of what's working.
overview.why_it_matters: Training systems currently track enrollment and certification but lose visibility the moment someone graduates. Real longitudinal outcome data is what actually proves (or disproves) a programme's value.
pain_points: Employment, retention, and wage-progression outcomes remain incomplete after training ends.
Trainees change contact details, employers report inconsistently, programmes use different identifiers.
Without longitudinal data, comparing providers or improving courses is difficult.
overview.background: Skilling programmes capture enrollment and certification well but lose track of real employment outcomes afterward, making it hard to evaluate programme effectiveness or target future investment.
overview.whats_being_asked: A longitudinal skilling-outcomes system with consent-based trainee records, automated/assisted follow-ups, employer validation, and cohort/provider/district analytics.
expected_solution: Consent-based, persistent trainee record linking training to outcomes.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Low-Moderate. Longitudinal outcome-tracking systems exist in other domains, applied here to a genuinely hard real-world tracking problem (contact changes, inconsistent reporting).
analysis.invention_effort_note: Very low as scored, achievable using structured follow-up and analytics patterns; the harder, less technical part is designing genuinely low-burden, privacy-conscious follow-up mechanisms.

competitive_landscape.note: Specific to skilling-outcome measurement, narrower field than generic survey/analytics platforms.

innovation.note: Established outcome-tracking pattern, real value in genuine low-burden follow-up design.

invention.note: Standard follow-up and analytics functionality, minimal technical complexity.

technical_feasibility.note: Fully achievable with realistic sample trainee/outcome data.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine value for programme evaluation, though the real impact only materializes over a longer measurement period than a hackathon can demonstrate.

architecture.note: Consent-based record system plus follow-up/analytics layer, low integration risk.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Yellow, undersold by tech-depth but genuinely useful for real programme evaluation. The real design challenge is genuinely low-burden, privacy-conscious follow-up, not the analytics layer, invest real design thought there.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Addresses a genuine, currently unmet evaluation need, without this, skilling programme effectiveness can't be reliably measured at all.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: A follow-up mechanism that's too burdensome or feels invasive will suffer poor response rates, exactly the problem this PS is trying to solve, design for genuine low-friction engagement.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Design your follow-up mechanism to be genuinely low-burden (SMS-based, short, infrequent) and explicitly consent-based, rather than a lengthy survey that would suffer the same poor-response problem as current methods.

idea_0_4: Design a genuinely low-burden, consent-based follow-up mechanism (short SMS-based check-ins are a reasonable approach).
Design your persistent trainee-identifier approach that survives contact-detail changes.
Split: one person on the record/consent architecture, one on the follow-up/analytics layer.
prototype_4_22: Build consent-based trainee record creation linked to training completion.
Build your low-burden follow-up mechanism (SMS-style check-ins at defined intervals).
integration_22_30: Connect records, follow-up, and validation into one coherent longitudinal tracking pipeline.
Test with a simulated multi-check-in timeline showing outcome data accumulating over time.
polish_30_36: Polish the follow-up experience for genuine low-friction engagement.
Rehearse a live demo showing the analytics dashboard populated from your simulated longitudinal data.
Prepare to discuss your consent and privacy design explicitly.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Demo your low-burden follow-up mechanism specifically, a quick SMS-style check-in, not a lengthy survey, and show how that design choice directly addresses the real-world response-rate problem current methods face.

strengths: Addresses a genuine, currently unmet programme-evaluation need.
Low technical risk, fully achievable with realistic sample data.
weaknesses: Real long-horizon impact can't be fully demonstrated in a hackathon timeframe, only the mechanism can be shown.
Genuine low-burden follow-up design is a real, easy-to-underestimate UX challenge.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Don't skip engagement design, that's what determines whether this actually solves the real-world response-rate problem.
team_fit.approach: Design your follow-up mechanism for genuine minimal friction from the start, this is the actual hard design problem.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing genuinely low-burden, privacy-conscious follow-up mechanisms and consent flows, that's real human-centered design judgment.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded generic survey-based follow-up system without genuine low-burden design would suffer the same poor response rates that make current outcome tracking incomplete.

data_resource_availability.status: No real trainee data should be used; realistic simulated longitudinal data is appropriate for a demo.

judge_qna.question: How do you actually get a good response rate to your follow-up, when this is the exact problem current methods fail at?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your specific low-burden design choices (short SMS check-ins, minimal effort required) and why they'd genuinely improve response rates over current methods.
judge_qna.follow_up: What response rate would you consider a realistic success threshold?

judge_qna.question: How does your persistent identifier survive a trainee changing phone numbers or locations?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your approach to identity persistence, whether through alternate contact capture, periodic re-verification, or another mechanism, and be honest about its real limitations.
judge_qna.follow_up: What happens when you genuinely lose contact with a trainee, how does that get reflected in your analytics rather than silently biasing the data?
